tagline: Wagon ruts from the Snake River ford to the Boise valley.
intro: The byway begins by looking for the ford. A short loop out of Glenns Ferry crosses the Snake River to the bluffs above Three Island Crossing and comes back to the state park on the north bank. Then county roads head northwest across the sagebrush desert beside the Oregon Trail itself, its ruts in sight along much of the way, to Bonneville Point southeast of Boise.

For its first ten years this was the trail's main line, and the freight and stage roads to the railroad in Utah used much of it for years after. Nearly every diarist wrote about the hot springs partway across, hot enough to cook fish and eggs. Irrigation wells dried them up.

moments.title: Three Island Crossing State Park
moments.text: Wagon ruts run between the Snake River and the park's history center, at a ford so feared that some emigrants stayed on the dry south bank instead.

moments.title: Canyon Creek Stage Station
moments.text: Emigrants called this Barrel Creek for its round valley inside rock walls, and the stone station built here in 1874 has been restored as one of two stage stops left on the trail.

moments.title: Bonneville Point
moments.text: From this ridge the emigrants got their first look at the Boise River and its cottonwoods, the first real trees in weeks, and concrete posts now mark the ruts.

practical: The byway roads are paved or good gravel and four-wheel drive is not needed, but there are no services on the stretches past Glenns Ferry, and BLM asks drivers to keep off the side access roads when they are wet or muddy.
